newsitem.title: USA: PaineWebber raises '97 nat gas price forecast.
newsitem.headline: PaineWebber raises '97 nat gas price forecast.

text.p: PaineWebber said on Wednesday it was raising its 1997 natural gas composite spot price forecast to a level well above current Wall Street consensus.
The firm raised the 1997 estimate to $2.30 per million British thermal unit from $2.05/MMBtu.
In a report, PaineWebber listed current First Call consensus at $2.14/MMBtu.

PaineWebber listed as reasons for the price forecast hike: a normal temperature outlook for the balance of the year, the current strength in spot prices, "less-than-ideal" amount of natural gas now in storage, the firm's expectation for record overall yearly demand, and limited near-term increases in overall deliverability, including from Canada.
As a result of the revisions, PaineWebber continues to recommend an overweighting in the (nat gas) group and raised its earnings and cash flow estimates for selective companies in the group.
Among those, PaineWebber raised its 1997 earnings estimate on Consolidated Natural Gas Co to $3.55 from $3.40, Sonat Inc to $2.90 from $2.55 and Louisiana Land and Exploration Co to $2.55 from $1.95.
PaineWebber's 1998 nat gas composite spot price forecast is $2.15/MMBtu, compared with First Call consensus of $2.04/MMBtu.
